title: Could You Fit 2 Million Hot Dogs Inside a Giant Sculpture? We Did the Math!
summary:
Picture a hot dog as long as a bowling lane—65 feet! That's the giant sculpture back in Times Square, New York City. It's called Hot Dog: The Second Serving, and it's part of America's 250th birthday celebration. Artists Jen Catron and Paul Outlaw made it. They even shoot confetti from inside the giant frankfurter!

But here's the fun part: how many real hot dogs could you stuff inside this monster? The inside is huge—about 6,000 cubic feet. That's like a room as big as three school buses. A normal Oscar Mayer hot dog is about 6 inches long and 1 inch wide, taking up about 4.7 cubic inches of space.

If you could magically pack them with no air gaps, you'd fit about 2.2 million hot dogs! But in real life, you can't squish them perfectly. There would be tiny empty spaces between each one. Experts say packing efficiency is about 80%—meaning 20% of the space is wasted. So a more realistic guess is around 1.75 million hot dogs. That's enough to give one to every person in a big city like Philadelphia!

Why does this matter? The artists used the hot dog to make people think about big ideas like American culture and how much we consume. But for us, it's just a super fun math puzzle. Next time you see a giant sculpture, try guessing how many things could fit inside!
why_it_matters: It shows how math can be used to answer fun questions about everyday things, like how many snacks could fill a giant object.

The hot dog is a popular American food often eaten at baseball games and summer cookouts.
Giant sculptures, like the Statue of Liberty (a gift from France for America's 100th birthday), are often made to honor important anniversaries.
